title: Phetchabun–Lopburi Road Trip: 3 Days, 2 Nights | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night Phetchabun–Lopburi driving plan in Thailand: Khao Kho and the misty hills, the Si Thep World Heritage city, then Lopburi the monkey town before heading back to Bangkok — with routes, timing, fees, and places that actually open.
keywords: Phetchabun Lopburi, Phetchabun Lopburi trip, Phetchabun to Lopburi route, Lopburi stopover, Si Thep World Heritage
h1:
Phetchabun–Lopburi
3 Days, 2 Nights on One Road
intro: Most people driving up from central Thailand to Phetchabun roll straight through Lopburi without noticing, because Highway 21 runs dead through Si Thep and Chai Badan on the way. So this trip strings the two provinces into a single line: head up to catch Khao Kho and its sea of fog, then on the way back stop at the Si Thep World Heritage site and spend a night in Lopburi the monkey town before reaching Bangkok — no backtracking.

blocks.html: Phetchabun and Lopburi sit on the same road, Highway 21. The distance between the two town centers is roughly 250 kilometers, about three and a half hours of driving if you don't stop. But there's plenty along the way that people later wish they'd pulled over for — the ancient city of Si Thep, recently named a World Heritage site, and Lopburi's old town, where you can spend a full day among monuments from the reign of King Narai. This plan keeps the drive up about the nature of Khao Kho, then works its way back down through history, finishing in Lopburi just two hours short of Bangkok.

blocks.title: Read before you set off
blocks.html: This trip suits people with their own car, because the sights are spread out beyond the town centers and there's no convenient public transport linking them. If you take the BKS 999 intercity bus, it does run through Si Thep–Nong Phai–Lom Sak, but stopping off along the way on your own is tough.

Starting from Bangkok or central Thailand, day one is a long drive up to Khao Kho in Phetchabun, with one night on the mountain. Day two is a full day around Khao Kho before easing south, stopping at Si Thep, then dropping down to sleep in Lopburi. Day three is walking Lopburi's old town in the morning, catching the sunflower fields or the Pa Sak dam mid-morning, then running into Bangkok in the afternoon. The whole trip comes to about 700 kilometers, but spread over three days it never feels like too much.

items: Day 1 — Bangkok → Khao Kho (drive ~5–6 hrs), overnight on the mountain
Day 2 — Around Khao Kho → down to Si Thep → overnight in Lopburi
Day 3 — Lopburi old town → Pa Sak dam / sunflower fields → back to Bangkok

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Phetchabun trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Phetchabun
items.note: Out and back in a day

items.activity: Leave Bangkok on Highway 1 through Saraburi, then turn onto Highway 21 toward Phetchabun
items.note: Fill the tank before getting onto Highway 21 — stations start thinning out after you pass Chai Badan

items.activity: Stop for lunch around Nong Phai or Bueng Sam Phan before reaching Phetchabun town
items.note: Plenty of noodle shops and rice-and-curry spots line Highway 21 here

items.activity: Climb Khao Kho via Highway 12, then branch onto 2196 — the road winds, so take it slow
items.note: With an automatic, use L or S to help brake on the descent

items.activity: Check in at your Khao Kho stay, drop your bags, then head out to a mountain-view café to catch the cool breeze
Find Khao Kho grilled pork or a local restaurant for dinner — when it's this cool, something hot hits the spot
items.note: See our Khao Kho grilled pork guide for the best spots

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Khao Kho in the morning, then down to Si Thep

items.activity: Up before dawn to a sea-of-fog viewpoint, such as Khao Kho viewpoint or Phu Thap Boek if you're staying nearby
items.note: The fog is clearest November–February — bring a warm jacket

items.activity: Back for breakfast at your stay, pack up, and check out
Stop at Wat Pha Sorn Kaew before heading down, to see the stained-glass hall on the hillside
items.note: Dress modestly — cover shoulders and knees before entering the temple grounds

items.activity: Down the mountain and onto Highway 21 heading south, with a meal stop around Bueng Sam Phan
Reach the ancient city of Si Thep in Si Thep district — walk Khao Khlang Nok, Prang Si Thep, and the Dvaravati-era monuments
items.note: Open 08:00–16:30 daily, 20 THB for Thai visitors; there's a tram tour around the site for an extra fee

items.activity: Leave Si Thep, continue south on Highway 21 toward Chai Badan, then into Lopburi town
items.note: Si Thep to Lopburi is about 100 km, around 1.5 hrs

items.activity: Check in at your Lopburi stay, find beef noodles or roast duck in town for dinner
items.note: The well-known spots around the Sa Kaeo roundabout stay open into the evening

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Lopburi old town, then back to Bangkok

items.activity: Start at Prang Sam Yot, the symbol of Lopburi — a Bayon-style Khmer tower with monkeys running all around
items.note: Keep valuables zipped away — the monkeys grab things, so don't walk around holding plastic bags

items.activity: Walk on to Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat, across from the train station, to see its corncob-shaped prang
items.note: It's an easy walk away, entry is a few tens of baht

items.activity: Visit King Narai's Palace, the royal residence from the reign of King Narai, and Vichayen House nearby
items.note: King Narai's Palace is closed Monday–Tuesday, so check ahead if you're going early in the week

items.activity: Lunch in the old town, then pick up some pla som fak (pickled fish) and dinso phong (soft chalk) to take home
Drive out to Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, or in winter swing by the sunflower fields around Phatthana Nikhom
items.note: The sunflowers bloom November–January, prettiest in the morning — by afternoon they may close up

items.activity: Head back to Bangkok via Saraburi onto Highway 1
items.note: Lopburi to Bangkok is about 150 km, around 2 hrs; to dodge Sunday-evening traffic, leaving before 3 pm is much smoother

blocks.text: What's worth stopping for along the way

blocks.html: If you've got time to spare or want to slow the trip down, Highway 21 has several more stops that don't take you far off the route. Slot them in whenever the pace feels right.

items.name: Si Thep Ancient City
items.blurb: Thailand's newest cultural World Heritage site, a Dvaravati city over a thousand years old. Khao Khlang Nok is the highlight — worth the walk up to see it.

items.name: Lopburi sunflower fields
items.blurb: Lopburi's winter landmark, whole fields of yellow blooms with mountains behind. Come in the morning when the flowers face the sun and look their best.

items.name: Pa Sak Jolasid Dam
items.blurb: The longest earthen dam in Thailand, with a tram running along the crest over wide reservoir views — a good place to stretch your legs before heading home.

items.name: Prang Khaek, Lopburi
items.blurb: The oldest Khmer tower in Lopburi town, sitting on a traffic island. A quick photo stop while you walk the old town.

items: Fuel up when you pass a bigger town — between Chai Badan and Si Thep stations start thinning out, so don't let the tank drop below half
The climb up Khao Kho is steep and winding — use a low gear to help brake, and avoid driving down the mountain at night if you're not used to it
Leave extra time on Sunday evenings — the run back into Bangkok gets busy around Saraburi, so leaving Lopburi before 3 pm flows better
Watch the monkeys in Lopburi — especially around Prang Sam Yot; don't leave food or bags anywhere a monkey can reach

blocks.title: You can trim it shorter
blocks.html: If you only have 2 days, drop Khao Kho: drive straight to Si Thep on the morning of day one, spend a night in Lopburi, then walk the old town on day two before heading back. You'll get a tight history trip that still covers the World Heritage site in full.

faq.q: How far is Phetchabun from Lopburi, and how long is the drive?
faq.a: Phetchabun town to Lopburi town is about 250 kilometers, roughly three and a half hours of driving if you don't stop. It's all one road — Highway 21 — straight down, passing through Si Thep district and Chai Badan.

faq.q: Should I visit Phetchabun first or Lopburi first?
faq.a: Coming from Bangkok or central Thailand, do the long drive up to Phetchabun and Khao Kho first while you've still got energy, then work your way back down through Si Thep and Lopburi on the return. That way you don't backtrack and you finish close to Bangkok.

faq.q: Where is Si Thep ancient city on the route, and is it easy to reach?
faq.a: Si Thep is in Si Thep district, Phetchabun province, right beside Highway 21 — so it's already on the Phetchabun–Lopburi line and easy to stop at. Open 08:00–16:30 daily, 20 THB for Thai visitors.

faq.q: What can I see in Lopburi in half a day?
faq.a: A morning is plenty to walk the old town. Start at Prang Sam Yot, continue to Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat, then visit King Narai's Palace and Vichayen House nearby, before lunch and picking up some souvenirs to take home.

faq.q: Can I do this trip without a car?
faq.a: You can, but it's hard work, because the sights are spread out and there's no convenient public transport linking them. If you really must, take the BKS 999 intercity bus that runs through Si Thep–Lom Sak, then rent a car or motorbike in each town.
